findings.title: Working-hours check uses start time for `end` and rejects slots when a day has several ranges
findings.body: `end` is computed from `slotStartTime`, so it is the same as `start`. The slot's end time is never checked against `endTime`. Also, `find` returns true as soon as any one working-hour entry fails the check. If a day has two entries (for example 9-12 and 14-17), a slot in one range is outside the other, so it is marked unavailable. Every slot is rejected on those days. Compute `end` from `slotEndTime`. Mark the slot unavailable only when no entry on that day contains it, for example with `some` to find a containing entry and a separate check that entries exist for that day.

findings.title: Date override check rejects slots when a day has several overrides, and the equality check is dead code
findings.body: The `find` returns true (slot unavailable) as soon as any override on that day excludes the slot. With two override ranges on one day (for example 9-11 and 14-16), a slot inside the first range is outside the second, so it is rejected. A slot must be rejected only if it fits none of that day's overrides. Also, `dayjs(a) === dayjs(b)` compares object identity and is always false. Use `.isSame()`, or drop the check. The zero-length override (day off) case is then not handled by this branch either, though the slot-before-start and slot-after-end checks may cover it.
